title: Changing a parameter changes the caller's variable
statement: A parameter is the same variable as the argument that was passed in, so assigning to the parameter inside the function changes the caller's variable, even for numbers and strings.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: trace a function that reassigns a primitive parameter
evidence_patterns.signature: reports the caller's variable as changed

example.item:
def bump(n):
    n = n + 1
x = 1
bump(x)
print(x)

discriminators.vs_slip: Consistent across items with primitive arguments. A slip is a single wrong trace.

vs.prog.func.argument-name-must-match-param: Name-matchers predict errors when names differ; aliasers accept different names.
vs.prog.obj.assignment-copies-object: The mirror: aliasers expect sharing where there is none; object-copiers expect independence where there is sharing. Test with a primitive item and a mutable-object item.

conflicts_with.label: Arguments are matched to parameters by position and copied in

resolved_by.label: Arguments are matched to parameters by position and copied in
Assignment copies a value into a variable at one moment
